Jewish households in Poland participated in town life and exchange and dealt with rulers and neighbors over residence, property and claims. Distant relatives could help communication and credit, while local protection, witnesses and performance remained necessary. Enforcers identified parties, disputed property and authority. Escort and custody consumed people, and excessive force could turn compensation claims into new injury and retaliation.
